sentences.text: Sefapanosaurus is a dinosaur distinguished by a cross-shaped astragalus bone in its ankle, a unique anatomical structure.
Its name combines the Sesotho word for 'cross' and the Greek word for 'lizard', while the specific name refers to the Zastron district where the type specimen was found.

Fossils, including a partial left foot and four partial skeletons, were excavated from the Elliot Formation in South Africa in the late 1930s and later held at the Evolutionary Studies Institute at Wits University.
Otero and colleagues formally described the genus in the June 23, 2015 issue of the Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society, establishing the binomial name Sefapanosaurus zastronensis.
Before this recent study, the remains were initially thought to belong to the genus Aardonyx.
Sefapanosaurus is considered a transitional genus between bipedal sauropodomorphs and giant quadrupedal sauropods.
The animal belongs to the order Saurischia and is classified within the suborder Sauropodomorpha, specifically grouped within the Sauropodiformes.

Fossils date to the Early Jurassic period, specifically the Pliensbachian stage, approximately 200 million years ago in what is now Africa, with a time range estimated from 227.3 to 199.5 million years ago spanning the Norian and Hettangian stages.
Sefapanosaurus was an early herbivorous sauropodomorph that lived in southern Gondwana, representing one of the first of its kind in the southern regions of the supercontinent.
